project.title: Age induced interactome remodeling in muscle mitochondria
project.projectDescription: A novel quantitative crosslinking mass spectrometry technique (qXL-MS) was applied to elucidate interactome changes in aged murine skeletal muscle mitochondria that contribute to age-related mitochondrial functional decline.  Reported here are results from initial investigations of murine muscle mitochondrial interactomes that enable identification of statistically significant changes associated with aging.  Newly developed isobaric quantitative protein interaction reporter (iqPIR) technologies15 enabled reproducible detection of age-related mitochondrial interactome changes.  Muscle mitochondria from young and old mice were isolated, cross-linked with iqPIR molecules, young and old mitochondrial samples were paired, process and analyzed to quantify age-related mitochondrial interactome changes.   In parallel, mitochondria were also subjected to additional measurements of mitochondrial protein yield, functional measurements including oxygen consumption rates on Complex I and Complex II substrates, and citrate synthase activity.
project.sampleProcessingProtocol: Gastrocnemius muscle was exised from hind legs of 4 old and 4 young mice; mitochondria was isolated and crosslinked with iqPIR reaent for quantitative XL-MS. Crosslinked mitocondira was lysed sni 8M urea, reduced with TCEP, alkylated with IAA, and protein concetration determined by Bradford assay. Equal amount of protein from one young and one old mitochondria were mixed, creating 4 bioloical replicates. Protein mixtures were digested with trypsin overnight, peptide desalted with SepPak columns and separated on a SCX column into 14 fractions to enrich for highly charged crosslinked peptides. Fractions were combined as follows: 1-5 (mostly linear peptides), 6-7, 8, 9, 10, 11-14. Combined fractions were incubated with monomeric avidin for 30 min at RT with shaking for enrichment of crosslinked, biotinylated peptides. Peptides were then dried down and resuspended in 30 uL of 0.1% FA. Samples were separated with RP on  Aquity HPLC (Waters) and anayzed on QExactive Plus (ThermoFisher Scientific). MS1 scans werecollected at 70K resolution, top 5  peaks with chare > 4 were selected for HCD fragmentation and MS2 were collected at 70K.
project.dataProcessingProtocol: Raw data files were converted to mzXML files and Mango software was used to select MS2 spectra with rlationships (peptide A + Peptide B + reporter = MS1 precursor). Spectra with relationship were searched against Mouse Mitocarta 2.0 database with Comet, and verified with XLinkProphet. iqPIR algorithm was used for quantitation and data was uploaded to XLinkDB with crosslink level FDR = 0.01.
